newsitem.title: USA: Snow, freezing rain hit northwestern U.S. Midwest.
newsitem.headline: Snow, freezing rain hit northwestern U.S. Midwest.

text.p: Snow and freezing rain were falling in the northern half of Iowa, as well as in Minnesota and northeast Nebraska, and forecasters were calling for the storm to persist through Tuesday morning.

"There's a chance of snow accumulation of one to three inches today (Monday) in northeastern Nebraska and a chance of three to five inches across Minnesota and Iowa," said Fred Gesser, chief forecaster with Weather Express in Omaha, Neb.
Low temperatures on Tuesday morning will dip below zero in North and South Dakota as well as Nebraska, Gesser said.

"We're looking at a pretty good-sized winter storm for Iowa, Minnesota and up into Wisconsin, now though early tomorrow (Tuesday)," said Craig Solberg, meteorologist with Weather Trades, Inc.in Des Moines.
Solberg said snowfall in those states could reach up to three to six inches.
Freezing drizzle and light snow were also forecast for states bordering the Great Lakes, but no significant snowfall was expected, the forecasters said.
Toward the end of the week, temperatures should warm up as a zonal system confines cold air to the Canadian Prairies, Gesser said.
"The trend is for warming during the (December) 26 through the 30," Gesser said.
